item.title: Giant phonon-assisted upconversion photoluminescence of in situ photo-carbonized polymer dots for 3D high-definition optical disks
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02004-z Researchers demonstrate high-capacity 3D optical data storage with high efficiency enabled by anti-Stokes phonon-assisted upconversion photoluminescence via in situ laser writing and reading of upconversion carbonized polymer dots.

item.title: Mapping one atom's interaction with light uncovers an unbounded network of quantum states
item.description: A new graph-theoretic framework provides a unified description of atom-light interactions across regimes ranging from weak to deep-strong coupling.

item.title: Magnetic order survives weak quantum fluctuations in gapless magnets
item.description: In a new study published in Physical Review Letters, researchers have shown that magnetic order can survive weak quantum fluctuations in disordered magnets that lack an energy gap. The work establishes robust ferromagnetism in the two-dimensional random-bond quantum Ising model, confirming a longstanding conjecture in quantum statistical mechanics.

item.title: Ultrathin materials could make quantum light circuits programmable
item.description: Quantum photonics could be a pivotal part of future quantum technology if the right materials can be created, a new review paper has found.

item.title: Attosecond current control and timing in a scanning tunnelling microscope
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02021-y Attosecond currents are induced by two-colour pulses in a scanning tunnelling microscope (STM) junction, enabling control of their direction and resolving thermal issues inherent to laser-driven STM. Sub-angström topographic sensitivity and 2-nm lateral spatial resolution are achieved.
